newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Forbes expects 26 pct rise in year profit.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Forbes expects 26 pct rise in year profit.

text.p: Forbes, the South African financial services group which lists on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday, said on Wednesday it expects attributable profit to rise 26 percent to 70 million in the year to March 31.
In its pre-listing statement published Forbes said the issue price of the shares, to be listed in the insurance sector, will be 535 cents each.
"This puts Forbes on prospective earnings and dividend yields of 6.5 percent and 3.2 percent respectively," the firm said. The forward price earnings ratio is 15.3 times.

Managing Director Paul Heinamann said good growth prospects existed for the group, whose two main businesses are employee benefits and actuarial consulting group Alexander Forbes, and risk management and insurance broking firm Price Forbes.
In the terms of the listing, shareholders in Servgro International Ltd, which owns 70 percent of Forbes, are being offered four new Forbes shares for every 100 Servgro shares held.

Institutions earlier this month eagerly snapped up a Forbes' tender offer to raise 60 million rand. The listing is expected to raise a total of 102.25 million rand which will be applied to developing the group's financial and professional services.
Forbes will be capitalised on the JSE at around 1.1 billion rand.
